package: @astryxdesign/cli

## astryx doctor

Diagnose Astryx projects and integration packages

Runs read-only project health diagnostics by default: Node version, @astryxdesign/core install and version alignment, theme packages, generated app themes when present, earlier copied-theme migration, config, integrations (every one astryx.config names must load, linked without a config entry, provider identity, contribution issues), agent docs, core peer dependencies, package manager, the docs the CLI reads, the newest release the computer knows of, with the install and upgrade commands when the project's release is older, and every `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12` command on the search path, warning when the first one is not the Astryx CLI or predates the hand-off. It writes nothing, but loading astryx.config runs that file's code. The `integration` subcommands provide authoring checks for one integration package. Outside a project it checks the computer instead: the Node version, the release that answered, the newest release this computer knows of, with the command that upgrades the CLI installed for the computer when it is older, the astryx commands on the search path, the integrations installed for the computer (warning about one it skips), and whether the computer-level agent text (`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 init --user`) is present, matches this release, was edited, or is turned off (info only); when that text names `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12` and no `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12` command is on the search path, apart from a package runner's own copy, it says so and names the install step the text records, or npm's when it records none. It never fails a check because the folder has no project.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor
```

Option           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`--built <path>` | Also check a finished build before you deliver it: a project folder, a build output folder, or one built HTML file. Fails when it does not use Astryx at all, and warns with each raw element, icon or custom style in its source.

```bash
# Run project diagnostics
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor
# Machine-readable project report
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor --json
# Before you deliver a build: check that it uses Astryx
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor --built dist
# Validate an integration
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor integration validate @acme/widgets
# Check template ids against Core
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor integration templates @acme/widgets
# Check component names against Core
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor integration components @acme/widgets
# Classify doc overlaps with Core
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor integration docs @acme/widgets
```

Exit code | When                                   
--------- | ---------------------------------------
0         | no checks failed (warnings are allowed)
1         | one or more checks failed              

Outside a project (`own`): it does what the description above says it does outside a project.

- `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor integration`: `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/doctor-integration`

It runs `doctor()` from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`. Read it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/api/functions/doctor`.

In global mode: outside a project, doctor checks your computer instead of a folder: `node-version`, `answering-release` (the version that answered), `newest-release`, `cli-on-path` (every astryx command on your PATH), `computer-integrations` (integrations installed globally), and `computer-agent-text` (the agent guide). It never fails a check because the folder has no project. In a project, the project's version of Astryx runs it, whichever astryx command you start. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global` and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/who-answers`.
